newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals sharply lower after US CPI.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals sharply lower after US CPI.

text.p: New York precious metals futures were sharply lower early Tuesday after the U.S. March CPI rose a less-than-expected 0.1 percent.

"There was some Australian producer selling overnight which started the latest slide, plus some sell stops were executed below $348.00 and then the U.S. CPI came in lower than expected, meaning real interest rates are even higher, making precious metals less attractive," North American Equity Services COMEX floor trader John Geraghty said.
COMEX June gold was down $3.00 at $345.70 an ounce after the first half hour of trade after setting a two-month low of $344.80.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $343.00/50, compared to the London Tuesday morning fix at $345.60 and the New York close Monday around $346.50/00.

Daily momentum indicators now have a negative tone, but many traders still think the range for spot gold for the next few months is likely to be limited to $340-360, with good physical demand seen at the bottom of the range and producer selling seen near the top.
COMEX May silver was down 4.3 cents at $4.680, after seeing an early low at $4.660, not far from the contract low at $4.655 seen on April 3.
Spot silver was quoted $4.67/4.69, also not far from three month lows around $4.65 seen in early January.
NYMEX July platinum was down $2.20 at $368.00, while NYMEX June palladium was down $4.15, with traders expecting talks on a resumption of Russian PGM supplies to Japan this month.
Short term palladium lease rates were reported to have slipped back under 10 percent Tuesday, after seeing a high around 16-20 percent last week.

"Once palladium on the TOCOM (Tokyo Commodity Exchange) overnight in the more active and distant months like December 1997 bell back under 600 yen a gram, selling became heavy and the lease rates eased," one refining source said.
February 1998 TOCOM palladium saw the most volume with 12,417 lots traded overnight and the contract fell 11 yen a gram to 595 yen.
